title: Zoox clears final federal hurdle to launch paid robotaxi service
excerpt: Federal safety regulators have given Zoox a temporary exemption that will allow the Amazon-owned autonomous vehicle technology company to charge customers for rides in its custom-built robotaxi.
content_html:
Federal safety regulators have given Zoox a temporary exemption that will allow the Amazon-owned autonomous vehicle technology company to charge customers for rides in its custom-built robotaxi.

The exemption from certain federal motor vehicle safety standards, which was announced Thursday by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), was one of the last remaining regulatory hurdles Zoox needed to clear before launching a commercial robotaxi service.

The decision was also published in the federal register.

Zoox custom-built vehicles lack many of the traditional controls required under federal law. For instance, the company’s autonomous vehicles do not have steering wheels or pedals. The agency is providing an exemption for eight federal motor vehicle standards, including windshield defrosting and light vehicle braking systems.

Nearly a year ago, the NHTSA gave Zoox an exemption that allowed it to demonstrate its robotaxis on public roads, and even give rides to passengers in cities like San Francisco and Las Vegas. But the company couldn’t charge customers for those rides.

This new exemption comes with a few guardrails. It limits Zoox’s commercial fleet up to 2,500 vehicles annually for two years. The company will also be subject to what the agency described as an “enhanced, adaptable oversight structure that can evolve as Zoox’s technology advances.”

A Zoox spokesperson told TechCrunch that the company will soon begin charging for its service, first in Las Vegas. Additional markets will follow as the company completes state-level requirements for commercialization, the company said. In California, where Zoox is headquartered, tests its AVs, and provides passengers with free rides, the company still needs driverless deployment permits from the state Public Utilities Commission and the Department of Motor Vehicles.

Zoox CEO Aicha Evans said the day marks an important milestone for the company and the future of autonomous mobility.

“We are honored to receive the first-ever commercial exemption for a purpose-built robotaxi from NHTSA, enabling us to begin charging for our service and take another step toward bringing autonomous ride-hailing to more communities,” Evans said in a statement.  

The Zoox news was part of a series of autonomous vehicle technology announcements made Thursday by the federal agency, including an update to the exemption process that allows automakers to temporarily sell a limited number of non-compliant vehicles, primarily to test new technologies.

The NHTSA said it is updating the exemption process to allow automakers to temporarily sell a limited number of non-compliant vehicles, primarily to test new technologies.

The agency also said it was partnering with SAE Industry Technologies Consortia, which will fund a three-year, $5 million consortium to gather data and accelerate creation of AV performance standards. The aim of the project, according to the NHTSA, is to create a single national standard for AV safety.

NHTSA Administrator Jonathan Morrison said in a statement that the agency supports the safe development and deployment of automated vehicles.

“By removing unnecessary barriers to innovation, developing industry guidance, and providing strong enforcement oversight while we create performance requirements, NHTSA is taking a balanced approach to AV regulation,” he said. “These advancements will ensure that the United States continues to lead the world in AV technology in a safe and responsible manner.”

The NHTSA also said Thursday it was reviewing an exemption application from Los Angeles-based startup Robomart for its low-speed driverless vehicle. The startup developed an autonomous delivery vehicle that can hold up to 500 pounds of goods. The NHTSA said it will publish a separate notice seeking public comment on its merits once the initial evaluation is complete.

Kirsten Korosec is a reporter and editor who has covered the future of transportation from EVs and autonomous vehicles to urban air mobility and in-car tech for more than a decade. She is currently the transportation editor at TechCrunch and co-host of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast. content_html_zh:
联邦安全监管机构已给予 Zoox 临时豁免，允许这家亚马逊旗下的自动驾驶汽车技术公司向客户收取乘坐其定制机器人出租车的费用。

美国国家公路交通安全管理局 (NHTSA) 周四宣布免除某些联邦机动车辆安全标准，这是 Zoox 在推出商业机器人出租车服务之前需要清除的最后监管障碍之一。

该决定也公布在联邦公报上。

Zoox 定制车辆缺乏联邦法律要求的许多传统控制措施。 例如，该公司的自动驾驶汽车没有方向盘或踏板。 该机构正在为八项联邦机动车辆标准提供豁免，包括挡风玻璃除霜和轻型车辆制动系统。

大约一年前，NHTSA 给予 Zoox 一项豁免，允许其在公共道路上展示其机器人出租车，甚至可以在旧金山和拉斯维加斯等城市为乘客提供乘车服务。 但该公司不能向客户收取这些游乐设施的费用。

这项新的豁免有一些限制。 两年内，Zoox 的商业车队每年的保有量不得超过 2,500 辆。 该公司还将受到该机构所描述的“增强的、适应性强的监督结构的约束，该结构可以随着 Zoox 的技术进步而发展。”

Zoox 发言人告诉 TechCrunch，该公司很快将开始对其服务收费，首先是在拉斯维加斯。 该公司表示，随着公司完成州级商业化要求，其他市场也将随之而来。 Zoox 总部位于加利福尼亚州，测试其自动驾驶汽车并为乘客提供免费乘车服务，但该公司仍需要获得州公用事业委员会和机动车辆部的无人驾驶部署许可。

Zoox 首席执行官 Aicha Evans 表示，这一天对于公司和自动驾驶的未来来说是一个重要的里程碑。

埃文斯在一份声明中表示：“我们很荣幸获得国家公路交通安全管理局针对专用机器人出租车的首次商业豁免，使我们能够开始对我们的服务收费，并朝着将自动驾驶叫车服务引入更多社区又迈出了一步。”

Zoox 消息是联邦机构周四发布的一系列自动驾驶汽车技术公告的一部分，其中包括更新豁免程序，允许汽车制造商暂时销售有限数量的不合规车辆，主要用于测试新技术。

NHTSA 表示正在更新豁免程序，允许汽车制造商暂时销售有限数量的不合规车辆，主要用于测试新技术。

该机构还表示，正在与 SAE 工业技术联盟合作，该联盟将资助一个为期三年、价值 500 万美元的联盟，以收集数据并加速创建自动驾驶性能标准。 根据国家公路交通安全管理局的说法，该项目的目的是为自动驾驶汽车安全制定单一的国家标准。

NHTSA 局长乔纳森·莫里森在一份声明中表示，该机构支持自动驾驶汽车的安全开发和部署。

他表示：“通过消除不必要的创新障碍、制定行业指南并在制定绩效要求的同时提供强有力的执行监督，NHTSA 正在对自动驾驶汽车监管采取平衡的方法。” “这些进步将确保美国继续以安全和负责任的方式在自动驾驶技术领域领先世界。”

NHTSA 周四还表示，正在审查洛杉矶初创公司 Robomart 为其低速无人驾驶汽车提出的豁免申请。 该初创公司开发了一款可承载 500 磅货物的自动送货车。 美国国家公路交通安全管理局表示，一旦初步评估完成，它将发布一份单独的通知，征求公众对其案情的评论。
